text:
Ellen: Noticed a janky UX in the compare table when filtering + toggling versions. On narrow screens the row virtualization unmounts rows and keyboard focus jumps to the top. Repro steps: open compare, apply 3 filters, press tab to focus pill row, use arrow to move, then apply a filter -> focus lost.

Ravi: Yikes. That will be bad for screen reader users too. We should implement a roving tabindex pattern so the focused pill stays consistent even if DOM nodes re-render. Also consider an aria-live region to announce the active filter count when filters change.

Kai: Agree on roving tabindex. Quick example for our React List virtualization (pseudocode):
```
// simplified
const [focusIndex, setFocusIndex] = useState(0)
// on keydown left/right: setFocusIndex(prev=>clamp(prev+-1))
// items render with tabIndex={i===focusIndex?0:-1}
```
Make sure to update focusIndex after virtualization recalc.

Anya: For performance badges: current design shows 5 metrics inline which causes huge row height on wrap. Proposal: reduce to 2 visible badges (latency, throughput) + a compact "more metrics" chevron that opens a popover with full list. That keeps density without removing access. Microcopy: change chevron tooltip to "View all performance metrics".

Ravi: A11y details: don't rely on the chevron alone. The popover trigger needs aria-expanded and aria-controls and the popover should manage focus trap and return focus to the trigger. For the aria-live announcements, prefer polite for filter counts and assertive for critical errors only. Also ensure live region doesn't flood when streaming metrics update rapidly—batch or debounce updates.

Ellen: Mobile behavior question: on small viewports should the pill row become a horizontal scroll or collapse into a single "Filters (3)" summary chip that opens a sheet? I lean summary chip for clarity.

Kai: Summary chip reduces visual noise and is easier to hit with a thumb on mobile. If we do horizontal scroll we must ensure inertia and keyboard compatibility (some mobile keyboards might switch focus unpredictably). Summary chip + sheet seems safer.

Anya: Pinning UX tweak: current label "Pin version" feels ambiguous. How about "Lock version in comparison"? Longer but clearer. Tooltip: "Lock this model version so it remains in the current compare set". Also, add a small visible state for pinned rows (subtle outline + pin icon) so users can scan quickly.

Ravi: Contrast/visibility: the thin outline we used for pinned state is low-contrast at 1px; bump to 2px or use a subtle background token. And ensure the pin icon has a title attribute for assistive tech.

Anya: I'll update the figma frames for both the desktop + mobile flows. Will include the roving-tab prototype and the 2-badge + more-popover treatment.

design-bot: Figma frames uploaded: https://www.figma.com/file/.../catalog-compare-accessibility-iter3 — comments enabled for @Ellen @Ravi @Kai.

Ellen: Thanks all. Plan: ship the a11y fixes + microcopy in the next minor, defer the mobile sheet polish to the next cycle. If anyone has final nits drop them here by EOD. :raised_hands:
